title: Calcutta High Court halts demolition of jailed Trinamool leader Jahangir Khan's Falta house
dek: Justice Suvra Ghosh asked how officials identified the house and ordered the state to file all video of the demolition, which began on Wednesday.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Calcutta High Court on Friday stopped the demolition of a house in Falta, South 24 Parganas, belonging to jailed Trinamool Congress leader Jahangir Khan, until the next hearing on Monday. Justice Suvra Ghosh also ordered the state to submit all video footage of the demolition, which district officials and police began at about 8.30 am on Wednesday.

The administration says the building, in Srirampur, stands on government land and that floors above the second were built without an approved plan. Mr Khan's family says the action is political.

## Questions from the bench

Justice Ghosh asked how officials had identified the house as Mr Khan's when he is in jail. "How did you identify the house? He is in jail now," the judge said, according to reports of the hearing. The judge also asked whether the required procedure had been followed, where the notice was, and why no independent witnesses had been present.

## The state's case

Advocate General Surajit Mitra told the court that two local residents had identified the house, according to reports. He said the notice had been sent by post and pasted on the wall of the building, that the owners had ignored seven-day notices, and that video of the process would be filed.

## The petitioner's case

Senior advocate Kishore Datta, appearing for the petitioner, said the notice was unsigned and that Mr Khan lived elsewhere. He told the court that demolition work had been speeded up, and the number of workers doubled, after the petition was filed, and called the action "political targeting", according to reports. He also alleged that lawyers in Diamond Harbour had been intimidated from taking up the case.

## Background

Mr Khan is a Trinamool leader from the Diamond Harbour area, the parliamentary constituency of party national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee. He is in custody. Demolitions of properties linked to Trinamool figures have become a running political dispute since the BJP came to power in the state this year. On Thursday the Kolkata Municipal Corporation removed a shed and gate from the footpath outside Mr Banerjee's Kalighat home, which he has taken to the Election Commission.

The BJP government says it is enforcing the law against illegal construction regardless of who owns it. The Trinamool says the demolitions are selective and meant to intimidate its workers.

In a separate development on Friday evening, Kolkata Police's Girish Park police station served a notice at Mr Banerjee's Kalighat home asking him to appear on 20 November, according to reports. The case stems from a complaint filed on 31 October over his remarks on 29 October that he would "settle scores" with police officers who, he alleged, were filing false cases against Trinamool workers at the government's instigation. Neither Mr Banerjee nor the Trinamool had responded to the notice by Saturday morning.

## What happens next

The stay holds until the hearing on Monday, 16 November, when the court will examine the notice and the footage the state has been asked to file.
